item.title: Re: HOT SIRENS IN YOUR AREA
item.content:encoded:
I hadn’t really considered that- originally I was just going to give the generic answer that they stole it, but that’s not very creative. I will probably drop the paratech in the final article.

And, yes! The ads wouldn’t strictly target people, but they would be ‘personalised’, in a sense. The images and text would change based on previous searches the user had made, and videos they’d clicked on. So, not to an anomalous degree- more like the kind of tracking that Amazon does to you. Which, y’know, still creepily accurate, but i’m pretty sure Jeff Bezos doesn’t have access to anomalous cookies.

Thanks for the crit! I really do appreciate it.

item.title: Re: HOT SIRENS IN YOUR AREA
item.content:encoded:
I actually like this one. You've taken an old critter and had some fun with it. It would be interesting to see the ads be a sort of cognitohazard, in that once someone sees an ad they are compelled to answer the ad and follow through on it.

This would force The Foundation to make a D-Class follow the ad, and then an MTF follow the D-Class to the sirens. Of course, this could create an interesting chase as the sirens see the MTF coming from a mile away. The Foundation would then administer some sort of anti-memetic to relieve the stress in the D-Class, who is unable to complete his quest.

Of course, the MTF could lose the D-Class, and when they followed the tracker find the corpse of the D-Class, forcing them to repeat the process until they find the sirens.

While I'm not sure you really need paratech here (the sirens' intent should be enough), another option would be to have the sirens run a newspaper and run the ads themselves. That not only gives them greater control over the ads, but also gives them a better lead time if someone starts investigating the ads.

You've got a great idea; I hope it works out!

item.title: HOT SIRENS IN YOUR AREA
item.content:encoded:
A coven of sirens- yes, like the mythological Greek kind- find themselves adapting to the modern climate in order to seek their prey.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre: Comedy, mainly, but not in an un-serious manner.

Elevator Pitch: You know those clearly fake ads you get on nsfw websites? The ones that’re like “HOT SINGLES IN YOUR AREA”, et cetera. Yeah. Those, but anomalous, and set up by Sirens, as in the type that’d lure sailors to death. The ad, if loaded on a page, would display a message along the lines of “10 HOT (xyz) WITHIN (distance)! TEXT NOW!”

+ show block
– hide block

As time went by, the distance would gradually decrease, and the number increase. This would culminate in the subject being ambushed, and then… well, consumed, by a number of horrible, vaguely humanoid fishy-people.

The Foundation would later track these ads to a certain location, and, unable to block the ads via webcrawlers or other non-anomalous means, would send in an MTF team to find out what’s going on. There’s an exploration log, and the anomaly is accidentally neutralised when the coven of sirens panics upon realising there’s angry fellows with guns in the hideout and collapses the building in order to escape, breaking all of their paratech that let them make and maintain the anomalous ads in the first place.

Central Narrative: The context behind this strange new manner of Greek monsters luring in prey is simply that people don’t usually fall for the ole’ “Sing to the sailors until they follow you and drown” trick, and they’ve had to resort to new and unusual means of tracking targets. Inkeeping with the tradition of luring sailors in with beautiful songs and false faces, they decide to essentially hijack NSFW spam ads, which ends up working pretty well.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: As far as I’m aware, nobody’s done sirens as an SCP before, and beyond that, the concept of the fake ads on the sides of sketchy sites actually being dangerous beyond just giving your computer malware is a little spine-chilling. And also really funny, when you think about it.

Additional Notes: As this would be my first SCP, essentially any critique at all would be greatly appreciated.
